editorial.headline: A Fixed-Premises Food Business, Fully Foreign-Open Nationally
editorial.standfirst: KBLI 56101 covers food-service operations from permanent premises, with a clear national opening to foreign investment and no Bali moratorium block at Large scale.
editorial.body:
KBLI 56101 is the framework for providing food to customers from a fixed, permanent building: a place that is not designed to be dismantled, moved or operated as a travelling venue. It encompasses table service where dishes are cooked to order, as well as counter and buffet formats where customers take, or are served, food already on display. Meals may be eaten on the premises, taken away, or delivered to the customer’s home. In practical terms, this is the home of restaurants, eating houses, canteens and cafeterias, fast-food restaurants, and take-away restaurants.

Its reach is deliberately broader than the classic street-facing dining room. A separately operated restaurant inside a hotel belongs here when it is not part of the hotel business itself. The same separate-unit principle applies to restaurants in transport facilities and aboard transport, as well as a take-away restaurant inside a supermarket. Catering restaurants and ice-cream or yoghurt outlets are also within the stated scope. The constant is not the menu or service style; it is an independently operated food-service business based in a fixed setting.

Registration is open at Mikro, Kecil, Menengah and Besar scale. Nationally, the activity is TERBUKA to foreign investment, with a foreign-ownership ceiling of 100%. That is a straightforward national position: a foreign investor can hold the entire permitted stake, rather than needing to infer a lower limit from the nature of a food business or from the way it serves customers.

Bali requires a more precise reading, but not a more pessimistic one. The province’s permanent moratorium blocks PMA registration for all Low and Medium-Low risk activities. This activity is not blocked by that rule: at Besar scale, its OSS risk is Menengah-Tinggi/Tinggi, and the Bali assessment is OK_or_HIGHER_RISK. For a foreign founder considering a fixed-premises food operation in Bali, the record therefore does not present a Bali moratorium prohibition. The national 100% foreign-ownership ceiling remains the relevant ownership position, while the Bali result is expressly one of no moratorium block at the stated risk profile.
